2026-08-27: rewriting the normal-list loop from an if-guarded do-while to a plain while loop with the loop-continuation test read ahead into unit_id at the bottom of the body (rather than re-testing *entry) eliminated the compiler's loop-carried value-forwarding artifact (a redundant unsigned ldrh plus manual lsls/asrs sign-extend on every iteration) for that loop, and also shrank candidate_bytes from 198 to exactly 194 (matching owner_bytes) as a side effect of the resulting register allocation; wrong_instructions fell 90 -> 80 from this change alone

2026-08-27: swapping the final selection multiply from `count * Random16()` to `Random16() * count` matched the reference's operand copy order (count copied into the accumulator register first) and dropped wrong_instructions 80 -> 60, differing_halfwords 69 -> 67

2026-08-27: the same while-loop-plus-read-ahead rewrite applied to the mirrored-list loop (with or without keeping its outer if-guard) consistently regressed wrong_instructions to 104+ and broke the otherwise-exact match on that loop's positions-pointer address computation (the sp+16-then-subtract-12 idiom); the mirrored loop's original if-guarded do-while, unmodified, remains strictly better and is retained

2026-08-27: the remaining 60 wrong instructions are almost entirely a single root cause -- the compiler keeps turn_order's dereferenced value in r3 (reusing the address-of-global scratch register) where the reference keeps it in r1 (treating r3 as a free scratch for immediate offsets throughout) -- which cascades into every downstream register choice; declaration-order changes, statement-order changes, and hoisting/duplicating index=0 were all tried and either had no effect or regressed, so this residual is register-allocation-level and no further permutation search is justified
